{
  "hook": "High-altitude slopes above Naoussa force Xinomavro to ripen slowly, locking in the sharp acidity and tight tannins that make Kir Yianni Ramnista age for decades. The Ramnista vineyard sits on iron-rich limestone and calcareous clay, a combination that strips excess vigor and concentrates tomato leaf, dried cherry, and olive notes into a structured, food-driven red.",
  "wine_summary": "Kir Yianni operates as a modern counterpoint to traditional Naoussa bottlings, applying precise temperature control and measured oak integration to a grape that historically required decades to soften. Ramnista translates the steep, northwest-facing slopes of Mount Vermio into a wine that balances aggressive tannic backbone with persistent savory fruit. The continental climate brings hot July days followed by sharp nighttime temperature drops, preserving malic acid in the berries and forcing the vine to push roots deep into fractured bedrock. That geological pressure shows up in the glass as a wine built for braised meats and long cellaring, not immediate consumption.",
  "terroir_expression": "The Ramnista vineyard occupies the western foothills of Mount Vermio, where calcareous marl and iron-rich red clay meet at elevations of 250 to 300 meters. Limestone fractures force root systems downward, restricting water access and naturally lowering yields to boost phenolic concentration. Summer heat builds sugar, but the sharp diurnal swing—often a 15°C drop after sunset—halts respiration and locks in tartaric acid. In the bottle, that geology translates to dried tomato, crushed rosemary, and a grippy, chalky finish that reads as pure limestone rather than fruit sweetness.",
  "vinification_summary": "Fermentation happens in temperature-controlled stainless steel, followed by 12 to 14 months in French oak barriques with roughly a third of the barrels being new. The winemaking team avoids excessive extraction, relying on punch-downs instead of pump-overs to keep the tannins structured but not green. They also complete malolactic fermentation, a biological process where bacteria convert sharp malic acid into softer lactic acid, which rounds out the palate without stripping the variety’s natural acidity. This measured approach prevents the wine from becoming overly oaky while still giving it enough structure to age gracefully.",
  "food_pairing": "- Slow-roasted lamb kleftiko with lemon and oregano: the wine’s high acidity cuts through the rendered fat, while the grippy tannins bind to the protein and soften on the palate.\n- Nashville hot chicken on white bread: the dried cherry and savory olive notes stand up to the cayenne heat, and the tartaric acid refreshes the mouth between fried bites.\n- Wild mushroom and fontina risotto: the earthy limestone finish mirrors the umami depth of the mushrooms, and the moderate alcohol won’t overwhelm the creamy starch.\n- Braised beef cheeks with sun-dried tomato ragù: the wine’s own dried tomato character creates a direct flavor bridge, while its firm structure holds up to the long-cooked collagen.",
  "comparable_wines": "Paolo Scavino Langhe Nebbiolo — shares the high-acid, high-tannin profile and dried tomato character typical of cool-climate calcareous soils.\nAlpha Estate Hedgehog Syrah — uses elevation and modern cellar techniques to tame powerful native fruit into age-worthy structure, mirroring Ramnista’s Macedonian roots.\nBodegas Muga Reserva Rioja — offers a similar balance of firm tannins, savory tertiary development, and oak integration at the same retail tier.",
  "style_profile": "Dry red with Xinomavro, medium body, high acidity, firm tannins, and a savory, limestone-driven finish.",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Store bottles horizontally at 55°F with stable humidity until the tannins begin to soften around year five. Open a young bottle with a full decant to accelerate integration, but hold back until at least 2022 for the 2017 vintage to show proper tertiary development.",
  "value_assessment": "At $29.50, this sits squarely against mid-tier Nebbiolo and aged Spanish Tempranillo, and it delivers better aging potential than either. You pay a premium for the precise cellar management and vineyard sourcing, but the cost undercuts comparable Greek single-vineyard bottlings by nearly ten dollars. It’s worth the shelf space if you want a structured, food-driven red that improves noticeably with five years of patience.",
  "market_position": "Restaurant sommeliers pull this bottle for Greek and Mediterranean menus where traditional pairings require high acid and firm structure. Retail buyers stock it as an entry point to age-worthy Greek reds, targeting home cellars and dinner-party hosts who want a conversation starter without chasing cult pricing. The consistent TEXSOM medal record has pushed it onto progressive wine lists that favor transparent, terroir-driven producers over heavily marketed international blends.",
  "insider_take": "Skip this if you want plush, fruit-forward reds ready to pour on a Tuesday night, but grab it immediately if you prefer wines that demand food and time. The trade-off is strict: young Ramnista tastes lean and austere, with tannins that grip the gums until oxygen and age soften them. Treat it like a young Barolo or a northern Rhône Syrah, and the dried tomato, olive, and mineral layers will reward the wait.",

  "drinking_window_min_years": 3,

parsed.hook: High-altitude slopes above Naoussa force Xinomavro to ripen slowly, locking in the sharp acidity and tight tannins that make Kir Yianni Ramnista age for decades. The Ramnista vineyard sits on iron-rich limestone and calcareous clay, a combination that strips excess vigor and concentrates tomato leaf, dried cherry, and olive notes into a structured, food-driven red.
parsed.wine_summary: Kir Yianni operates as a modern counterpoint to traditional Naoussa bottlings, applying precise temperature control and measured oak integration to a grape that historically required decades to soften. Ramnista translates the steep, northwest-facing slopes of Mount Vermio into a wine that balances aggressive tannic backbone with persistent savory fruit. The continental climate brings hot July days followed by sharp nighttime temperature drops, preserving malic acid in the berries and forcing the vine to push roots deep into fractured bedrock. That geological pressure shows up in the glass as a wine built for braised meats and long cellaring, not immediate consumption.
parsed.terroir_expression: The Ramnista vineyard occupies the western foothills of Mount Vermio, where calcareous marl and iron-rich red clay meet at elevations of 250 to 300 meters. Limestone fractures force root systems downward, restricting water access and naturally lowering yields to boost phenolic concentration. Summer heat builds sugar, but the sharp diurnal swing—often a 15°C drop after sunset—halts respiration and locks in tartaric acid. In the bottle, that geology translates to dried tomato, crushed rosemary, and a grippy, chalky finish that reads as pure limestone rather than fruit sweetness.
parsed.vinification_summary: Fermentation happens in temperature-controlled stainless steel, followed by 12 to 14 months in French oak barriques with roughly a third of the barrels being new. The winemaking team avoids excessive extraction, relying on punch-downs instead of pump-overs to keep the tannins structured but not green. They also complete malolactic fermentation, a biological process where bacteria convert sharp malic acid into softer lactic acid, which rounds out the palate without stripping the variety’s natural acidity. This measured approach prevents the wine from becoming overly oaky while still giving it enough structure to age gracefully.
parsed.food_pairing:
- Slow-roasted lamb kleftiko with lemon and oregano: the wine’s high acidity cuts through the rendered fat, while the grippy tannins bind to the protein and soften on the palate.
- Nashville hot chicken on white bread: the dried cherry and savory olive notes stand up to the cayenne heat, and the tartaric acid refreshes the mouth between fried bites.
- Wild mushroom and fontina risotto: the earthy limestone finish mirrors the umami depth of the mushrooms, and the moderate alcohol won’t overwhelm the creamy starch.
- Braised beef cheeks with sun-dried tomato ragù: the wine’s own dried tomato character creates a direct flavor bridge, while its firm structure holds up to the long-cooked collagen.
parsed.comparable_wines:
Paolo Scavino Langhe Nebbiolo — shares the high-acid, high-tannin profile and dried tomato character typical of cool-climate calcareous soils.
Alpha Estate Hedgehog Syrah — uses elevation and modern cellar techniques to tame powerful native fruit into age-worthy structure, mirroring Ramnista’s Macedonian roots.
Bodegas Muga Reserva Rioja — offers a similar balance of firm tannins, savory tertiary development, and oak integration at the same retail tier.
parsed.style_profile: Dry red with Xinomavro, medium body, high acidity, firm tannins, and a savory, limestone-driven finish.
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Store bottles horizontally at 55°F with stable humidity until the tannins begin to soften around year five. Open a young bottle with a full decant to accelerate integration, but hold back until at least 2022 for the 2017 vintage to show proper tertiary development.
parsed.value_assessment: At $29.50, this sits squarely against mid-tier Nebbiolo and aged Spanish Tempranillo, and it delivers better aging potential than either. You pay a premium for the precise cellar management and vineyard sourcing, but the cost undercuts comparable Greek single-vineyard bottlings by nearly ten dollars. It’s worth the shelf space if you want a structured, food-driven red that improves noticeably with five years of patience.
parsed.market_position: Restaurant sommeliers pull this bottle for Greek and Mediterranean menus where traditional pairings require high acid and firm structure. Retail buyers stock it as an entry point to age-worthy Greek reds, targeting home cellars and dinner-party hosts who want a conversation starter without chasing cult pricing. The consistent TEXSOM medal record has pushed it onto progressive wine lists that favor transparent, terroir-driven producers over heavily marketed international blends.
parsed.insider_take: Skip this if you want plush, fruit-forward reds ready to pour on a Tuesday night, but grab it immediately if you prefer wines that demand food and time. The trade-off is strict: young Ramnista tastes lean and austere, with tannins that grip the gums until oxygen and age soften them. Treat it like a young Barolo or a northern Rhône Syrah, and the dried tomato, olive, and mineral layers will reward the wait.
